problem: touching_merges always returns True, so merge joins intervals meeting at a point both exclude (e.g. [0,1) and (1,2] become [0,2]), inventing that point in normalize and union results.
difference's final merge rejoins the pieces around a removed point, so difference([(0,2)],[(1,1)]) returns [(0,2,True,True)] and removing a single point does nothing.
intersection merges each input before comparing them, so a point neither input contains can appear in the result (intersection([(1,1)], [0,1)∪(1,2]) returns [(1,1)]).
The change deletes the docstring stating the merge rule, leaves both parameters unused, and adds no tests, so nothing catches the regressions at the shared-endpoint boundary.
